_readme:
The format library — organic structures reverse-engineered from the owner's own swipes, each one carrying the post that proved it and its view count. A format is the STRUCTURE (camera, text behaviour, beat order, what carries the value), never the topic. Brand-agnostic by design: the brand enters at injection, per workspace rule 7. Seeded 2026-08-31 from the top swipes read frame-by-frame; the classifier assigns these and may propose a new one, which enters here only after a human read. Settled again 2026-09-04 by the second consolidation pass: 116 proposed ids were reduced onto 48 canonical structures — the 34 the library already carried, kept as they were, plus 14 promoted here — merging only on the four axes (camera behaviour, text behaviour, beat order, and what carries the persuasion) and never on topic. Genuine one-offs stayed out and are still tagged as proposed; the merge map is records/format-merges.json. Extended 2026-09-11 with the first entries that did not come from swipes: the asset index read 1,342 clips of our OWN delivered footage against this library and 82 came back unlisted. Two structures cleared a read and are filed here as state 'proposed', source 'owned-footage' — operator-service-montage and stranger-answer-montage. They carry that provenance because a structure seen in a stranger's post and one seen in footage we commissioned are different claims, even when they look identical. The rest of the 82 stay as candidates in tools/asset-index/findings/format-candidates.md.

STATUS, added 2026-09-11 (the owner: "before you go to the format library, that needs to be organized and audited too"). Every entry now carries `status` and `signed`, the same discipline the angle bank uses, and a `proof` block naming how many posts are actually behind it. 48 of the 50 rest on ONE post — a shape seen once, however large its view count, is a shape seen once. Nothing here is `active` until the owner signs it; `unreviewed` is the honest default and is not a demotion. Since 2026-10-07 (components rule 6, triage page 15) `status` is draft / approved / deprecated only; `unreviewed` and `proposed` are an entry's `state`, beside status `draft`.

FAMILIES, added 2026-09-11, and RULED the same day. I read three sets as near-duplicates of one mechanic and proposed collapsing them. the owner, having seen the library render for the first time: "Technically, all of these are unique formats." They are. A `family` groups entries that share a TEXT MECHANIC — it is a way to browse fifty entries, never a merge list, and no entry is a candidate for deletion because of it. What the grouping is genuinely good for is spotting that seven different formats all rest on the same text behaviour, which is a fact about the lane, not a fault in the bank. Separately, every entry carries `text_mechanic` — across the whole library there are only six.

formats.name: Sticky-line maker demo
formats.mechanic: One text line pinned for the ENTIRE runtime while one continuous handheld demonstration plays out. The line never changes, so nothing competes with the product; the viewer re-reads it while watching hands work. Face is cropped or incidental — the maker is a pair of hands, not a personality.
formats.why_it_works: No cut to a talking head means no permission needed to keep watching. The unchanging line acts as the promise; every second of footage is evidence against it.
beats: unbox or unwrap the product, hands only, real room — or open straight into use
unfold / assemble — the scale reveal
place it where it lives (bed, counter, floor)
use it as intended, one unbroken take
close on the mechanism (switch, controller, texture) — the proof detail
formats.text_behaviour: one line, top third, same words start to finish, casual + an emoji or two; some instances land the line once on the opening beat and drop it, which does not break the format — what matters is that the text never changes and never argues
formats.camera: handheld phone, vertical, subject-height, natural window light, no cuts to face

formats.mechanic: A camera that never moves, held on the thing being treated. ONE WORD per beat builds a sentence across the whole video, one step of the procedure per word. word 6 — hands finishing, the result held for a beat

formats.camera: zero camera movement — usually locked overhead on a reclined or seated subject, sometimes a locked frontal frame with the problem held at the edge of shot; even indoor light

formats.mechanic: One continuous narration is chopped into per-beat caption fragments that never complete a sentence, and that running caption is the only thing holding together footage the creator did not shoot — someone else's clip, a published diagram, a screen recording, stock process footage. formats.mechanic: The creator states the question to camera, then approaches strangers in public and lets their unscripted answers carry the whole argument. Every word is burned in as rolling captions because the audio is street audio. The creator never makes the claim — the strangers make it for him, and the more reluctant or unpolished they sound, the better it works.
formats.why_it_works: The persuasion belongs to people with nothing to gain. A creator saying women notice your skin is an ad; four strangers saying it unprompted is evidence. The awkwardness is load-bearing — a stranger hesitating, or giving a blunt answer the creator did not want, is the proof that nothing was scripted.
